reading.body:
H.R. 9914 has 23 cosponsors, 13 Republicans and 10 Democrats, and no lobbying filing from 2025 or later names it.

The cosponsor list is the whole of the data. It is bipartisan and it is large for a single bill, which is the one pattern worth noting. The bill's own text is tagged with jobs and workforce, frontier safety, and national security and exports, so the coalition spans members whose districts and committee seats touch workforce programs, defense and export control, and technical standards. Robert Latta sponsors it, and the cosponsors include Jay Obernolte, Ted Lieu, Bill Foster, and Raja Krishnamoorthi, members who recur on technology files.

For AI specifically, the absence of lobbying filings is the more informative fact. A bill that would draw industry money would show filings naming it, and none do. That does not mean industry is indifferent, because a filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken, and the absence of filings shows only that no filing names it. It does not tell the reader what the bill would do, what its status is beyond a latest status date of 2026-07-23, or whether it will move. Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power, and the data does not support drawing that connection.

summary: H.R. 9914, Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act. Latest status date 2026-07-23. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: jobs and workforce, frontier safety, national security and exports. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
